chunks: One obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj is better than a house filled with gold that is given in charity until nothing remains.

key_terms.بَيْتٍ: a house, used here to express great quantity
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: better; superior in merit and reward
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ: twenty, indicating a large multiplied comparison

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith compare the virtue of obligatory salat (prayer), hajj, and charity?
ai.summary: This narration emphasizes the immense merit of an obligatory salat (prayer), placing it above numerous hajj pilgrimages. It also highlights the greatness of hajj, ranking it above immense charitable giving, thereby underscoring the lofty station of divinely prescribed acts of worship.
